data.why: The interface has no file-upload widget; a scientist pastes a gene (or GO id) list into a textarea, so these repo-bundled test lists (clean human list, a mixed symbol/GO-id/invalid-symbol list, a mouse-only list, and a pure GO-id list) give realistic paste-in content plus the edge cases (unknown symbol 'FOO', a GO id mixed with genes) the filters are meant to handle.

goals: paste a list of genes and draw the shared Gene Ontology (GO) subgraph that connects their annotated functions
raise or lower the minimum coverage filter to find functions shared by the most genes in the list versus rare, specific ones
apply a word/regex filter on the Function column to narrow the tree to a biological theme (e.g. 'kinase' or 'lipid')
restrict the view to one GO domain (Biological Process, Molecular Function, or Cellular Component) to inspect a single branch
switch the organism database (human, mouse, rat, fly, zebrafish, worm, e.coli, yeast, arabidopsis) to annotate a gene list from a different species
download the resulting annotation table as CSV or the graph as a DOT file for use outside the interface

review.summary: The tree captures GeneScape's purpose and stages well: paste a list, pick the organism, draw the GO subgraph, narrow it by coverage, regex and domain, read the table, and export. Its general and specific labels are clean, and 12 of 13 sampled screens support their nodes. Before it is filed, it needs one corrected citation (the hover on 041), the one-identifier-per-line limit, a task for reading node specificity, and Domain moved into the filtering phase and given a feature.
